package_info.package_manager: IPFS (decentralized web deployment of JavaScript UI)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is malicious because a developer surreptitiously inserted JavaScript code into the Tornado Cash user interface that exfiltrates users' private deposit notes (which function as private keys) to an external server, enabling theft of user funds. This code was hidden in a governance proposal and affected all users accessing the UI via IPFS gateways.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, specifically when a user initiates a deposit or withdrawal action in the UI
execution_context.file_location: JavaScript UI codebase, likely within the main application logic handling deposit/withdrawal (e.g., src/app/DepositWithdraw.js or a related utility module)
required_permissions: Network access to make outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests
Access to in-memory deposit notes (private keys) generated or handled during user actions

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user performs a deposit or withdrawal, the code captures the user's private deposit note, encodes it using encodeURIComponent, and sends it via an HTTPS POST request to an attacker-controlled external server, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is suspicious because it covertly captures sensitive user secrets (deposit notes/private keys) and transmits them to an external, attacker-controlled server without user knowledge or consent, directly enabling theft of user funds.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Tornado Cash UI code should never transmit private deposit notes or keys off-device; all cryptographic operations and secret handling are expected to remain strictly local to the user's browser and device.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry might send anonymized, non-sensitive usage data, but there is never a valid reason for the UI to transmit private keys or deposit notes to any external server.
key_indicators: JavaScript code that accesses or serializes deposit notes or private keys during sensitive wallet operations
Outbound network requests (e.g., fetch or XMLHttpRequest) to untrusted or non-official external domains during deposit or withdrawal actions
Encoding of sensitive data (such as encodeURIComponent or base64) immediately prior to network transmission
Presence of hardcoded external URLs or domains in code paths handling user secrets

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is inserted into the Tornado Cash UI codebase via a deceptive governance proposal, introducing code that exfiltrates deposit notes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of the compromised UI to public IPFS gateways

attack_chain.action: Users access the compromised Tornado Cash UI through IPFS gateways (such as ipfs.io or cf-ipfs.com), unknowingly loading the malicious code in their browsers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious code in users' browsers during normal UI interactions

attack_chain.action: When users perform deposit or withdrawal actions, the malicious code captures their private deposit notes from memory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive secrets are prepared for exfiltration

attack_chain.action: The captured deposit notes are encoded and sent via HTTPS POST requests to the attacker's external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives the exfiltrated deposit notes and can use them to access and drain user funds from Tornado Cash

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that accesses or serializes deposit notes or private keys during deposit or withdrawal operations
Outbound network requests (POST or GET) to external domains not officially associated with Tornado Cash, especially during sensitive wallet actions
Encoding of sensitive data (e.g., encodeURIComponent, base64) immediately before network transmission
Presence of hardcoded external URLs or domains in code paths that handle user secrets
file_indicators: Unexpected or unauthorized changes in Tornado Cash UI JavaScript files, particularly in modules handling deposit/withdrawal logic (e.g., src/app/DepositWithdraw.js)
Obfuscated or newly added code introduced via governance proposal merges, especially in files related to user secret handling
References to external or suspicious domains in network request code within the UI codebase
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests from the UI to domains not associated with Tornado Cash (e.g., attacker-server.com/collect) during deposit or withdrawal actions
Unusual traffic from user browsers to unknown endpoints coinciding with deposit or withdrawal operations
Network requests containing encoded or serialized deposit notes or private keys in the payload
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor the Tornado Cash UI codebase for any logic that accesses deposit notes or private keys and transmits them over the network. Flag any JavaScript code that encodes and sends sensitive data to external domains, especially in modules handling deposit or withdrawal. On the network side, detect and alert on POST requests from the UI to domains not officially associated with Tornado Cash, particularly during user deposit or withdrawal actions. Review governance proposals and code merges for hidden, obfuscated, or unauthorized code that could perform exfiltration of user secrets.
